subs.text: Book six.
The Princess and the Stranger.
Scene one.
Athena Enters Nausicaa's Dream.
Athena reaches the palace of Alcinous and enters Nausicaa's chamber in the likeness of a friend.
Athena reproaches the princess for leaving fine clothes unwashed before marriage.
Papa dear, will you not have the high wagon yoked for me,
so I can take our fine clothes to the river and wash them?
You yourself need clean linen for the council,
and five sons in this house are forever wanting fresh things for the dancing.
Neither mules nor anything else do I grudge you, child.
Go —
the servants will yoke the high wagon, the one with the box for the wash.
Her mother packs food, wine, and oil.

scenes.title: The Naked Stranger Emerges
scenes.card: Naked and salt-caked, Odysseus covers himself with a branch and begs Nausicaa for help; her maids flee but she stands firm.

subs.text: Scene three.
The Naked Stranger Emerges.
Odysseus debates whether to clasp Nausicaa's knees or speak from a distance.
Breaking a leafy branch to shield his body, he steps out salt-crusted and terrible,
like a mountain lion driven by hunger down among the flocks.
The maids flee, but Athena keeps Nausicaa steady.
At your knees, lady —
though I dare not touch them —
tell me:
are you goddess or mortal?
Never have my eyes seen your like, and I have suffered:
long days the sea broke over me, and I know not one soul in this land.
Pity a stranger —
grant me some cast rag to wear, and show me the way to your town.
Stranger, you seem neither base nor witless, and Zeus deals fortune as he wills —
what he gives, a man must bear.
But you have come to our land now,
and you shall lack neither clothing nor anything owed a hard-tried suppliant.
Stand, girls —
this man is no enemy;
wash him where the river gives shelter, and set food and oil beside him.

scenes.title: Bath, Clothing, and the Road to Town
scenes.card: Washed and dressed, Odysseus looks splendid; Nausicaa tells him to follow her to town and plead first with the queen.

subs.text: Scene four.
Bath, Clothing, and the Road to Town.
The maids set food, the golden flask of oil, and clothing beside the eddying river,
and withdraw while he washes the crusted brine from his back and shoulders.
Athena makes him appear taller, stronger, and more radiant.
Nausicaa admires him.
Nausicaa eats while the women fold and load the dry clothes.
Rise now, stranger, and follow while we cross the fields —
but when we near the town, wait in Athena's grove of poplars until you judge we have reached my father's house,
so no sailor's idle tongue can shame me.
Then come into the city and ask for the palace of great-hearted Alcinous;
walk straight through the hall and clasp the knees of my mother Arete first.
Win her heart, and you may hope to look on your home and your own people again.
